## B — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

Audience: first-time passenger-car applicants studying basic vehicle control and hazard scanning in the mapped New Mexico handbook scope.
Level: introductory written-knowledge preparation; practical driving instruction, motorcycle operation and commercial licensing are outside this map.
Prerequisite: work from the source-backed terminology and conditions indexed in the knowledge parts; official exam weight is unknown (verify NM-SEC08-AUDIENCE).
Grouping and difficulty are pedagogic hints only; this dossier does not claim an official question distribution.

sections.heading: C — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning
sections.markdown:
## C — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Learning to drive safely requires instruction and practice beyond reading a manual. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Use the vehicle owner’s manual for the proper starting procedure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Before starting the vehicle, make sure its parking brake is applied. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
A manual-transmission vehicle must be out of gear before starting. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Some manual-transmission vehicles also require pressing the clutch before starting. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A01
Before starting an automatic-transmission vehicle, select Park. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A01
Build speed smoothly rather than accelerating abruptly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A01
A sudden start can spin the driving wheels and make the vehicle slide, especially on a slick surface. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A01
With a manual transmission, practice coordinating clutch and accelerator to avoid over-revving or stalling during gear changes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A01
Grip the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides in a balanced position. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A01
The staged handbook presents the ten-and-two clock positions as a balanced steering grip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A01
The handbook also describes the nine-and-three clock positions as an alternative grip. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A01
Keep your knuckles on the outside of the steering-wheel rim. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A02
Look far ahead and toward both roadsides so upcoming steering needs can be recognized early. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A02
For a sharp corner, the handbook describes using hand-over-hand steering. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A02
After completing a turn, guide the wheel back to straight by hand. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A02
Allowing the steering wheel to slide through your fingers can be dangerous. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A02
Check the speedometer frequently because a driver’s sense of speed is unreliable. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A02
After leaving a fast road for a slower local road, a driver can underestimate the vehicle’s speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A02
Follow the posted speed-limit signs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A02
Look for the need to stop early instead of waiting for a last-second response. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A02
Abrupt braking can produce a skid and loss of vehicle control. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A02
A sudden stop makes it harder for following drivers to stop without hitting your vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A02
Recognizing hazards early allows a gradual slowdown or lane change instead of a panic stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A02
Scan in front, on both sides and behind the vehicle to stay aware of surrounding events. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A02
Scanning helps identify people or vehicles that could enter your path before you reach them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A02
Scanning also reveals warning signs and route directions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A02
Looking well ahead reduces the need for a last-moment turn or brake application. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A02
Looking well ahead can help conserve fuel and keep traffic movement steady. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A02
Far-ahead scanning helps a driver steer with less weaving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A02
The handbook says safer drivers tend to look at least ten seconds ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A02
In city traffic, the handbook’s ten-second look-ahead distance is approximately one block. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A02
The handbook recommends looking at least a block ahead in city driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A02
Look toward both sides for entering vehicles or pedestrians, especially near intersections and railroad crossings. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A03
An intersection is any point where traffic paths join or cross, including streets, driveways and parking-lot entrances. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F36 | anchor: A03
Before entering an intersection, look left and right for traffic and pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F37 | anchor: A03
After stopping at an intersection, look both ways again just before moving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F38 | anchor: A03
Before moving into an intersection, confirm the entire crossing path is clear so a stop will not block it. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-F39 | anchor: A03
Before entering an intersection, make sure you can clearly see traffic crossing your path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

Misconceptions: mirrors do not reveal every blind spot, and a green signal does not guarantee an empty intersection.
Mnemonics: ahead, sides, behind keeps the scan moving through the surroundings.
Glossary: scanning means checking the surrounding traffic picture; blind spots are areas the mirrors cannot show.
Dynamic facts: the owner’s manual supplies vehicle-specific startup details; current road activity determines where hazards emerge.

sections.domain: Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning
sections.heading: C2 — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Basic vehicle control and hazard scanning

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A03
Before turning left across approaching traffic, wait for a gap large enough to complete the movement safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A03
Before turning left, check the destination street for vehicles or pedestrians that could leave you stranded in the opposing traffic path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A03
Immediately before a left turn, check the approaching traffic direction once more. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A03
Before turning right, check for vehicles approaching from your left. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A03
Before turning right, check whether an oncoming vehicle will turn left into your path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A03
Check for pedestrians in the destination crossing before beginning a right turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A03
A posted prohibition overrides the handbook’s permission to turn right on red. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A03
The handbook allows a turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street unless that left turn is prohibited. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A03
Do not assume a traffic sign or signal guarantees that cross traffic will stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A03
Look left and right at an intersection even when crossing traffic faces a red light or a stop sign. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A03
Use particular care just after a light turns green because cross traffic may still try to hurry through. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A03
If your cross-street view is blocked after stopping, creep forward slowly until approaching traffic becomes visible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A03
Moving forward slowly lets crossing drivers see your vehicle’s front early enough to slow or warn you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A03
Scan the roadside carefully near shops, parking lots, road work, busy sidewalks, playgrounds and schoolyards because people may enter the road there. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A03
At every railroad approach, reduce speed and look both ways along the tracks for a train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A03
A crossing where you have never seen a train must still be checked for an approaching train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A03
Cross tracks only when enough room exists beyond them to hold the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A03
At a multitrack crossing, let a passing train move well away before crossing because it can hide another train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A03
Monitor rear traffic more frequently when the traffic stream is heavy. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A03
Rear checks reveal a following vehicle that is too close or approaching too quickly. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A03
Rear-traffic checks are especially important before a lane change, slowdown, backing movement or descent of a long or steep hill. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A03
Before changing lanes, check both the side and the rear for vehicles in the intended lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A03
Lane changing includes merging from an entrance ramp and entering traffic from a curb or shoulder. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A03
Use both rearview and side mirrors to check whether the target lane is clear. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A03
Before changing lanes, make sure another vehicle is not about to pass you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A04
Before moving sideways, look over your shoulder toward that direction to check near the vehicle’s rear corners. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R27 | anchor: A04
The rear-corner areas invisible through the mirrors are blind spots. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R28 | anchor: A04
Side and rear checks should be brief because traffic ahead can stop unexpectedly while you look away. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R29 | anchor: A04
Use mirrors while preparing to merge, change lanes or enter the road so you can continue monitoring ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R30 | anchor: A04
Check over your shoulder for blind-spot traffic immediately before changing lanes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R31 | anchor: A04
Several quick looks are preferable to one long look away from the road ahead. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R32 | anchor: A04
During a lane change, track both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the lane you are entering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R33 | anchor: A04
Check the lane beyond your target lane because another driver may be moving into the same space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R34 | anchor: A04
Motorcyclists, bicyclists and pedestrians can be harder to notice than cars or trucks. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R35 | anchor: A04
Be particularly alert for other road users when pulling into the roadway from a curb or driveway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R36 | anchor: A04
Check rear traffic whenever you slow, especially for a sudden slowdown or a stop at an unexpected driveway or parking space. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R37 | anchor: A04
Keep backing movements to a minimum because the area behind a vehicle is difficult to see. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R38 | anchor: A04
A parking space that lets you drive through can allow a forward departure instead of backing out. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R39 | anchor: A04
Before entering the vehicle to back it, check behind for children or low objects hidden from the driver’s seat. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R40 | anchor: A04
When backing, the handbook describes resting the right arm on the seatback and turning to look through the rear window. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R41 | anchor: A04
Do not rely only on the mirrors while backing because they do not show the area directly behind the vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R42 | anchor: A04
Reverse slowly because controlling the steering is harder while moving backward. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R43 | anchor: A04
Use a person outside to help guide a backing movement whenever possible. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R44 | anchor: A04
During a long or steep descent, watch the mirrors for vehicles gaining speed behind you. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec08-R45 | anchor: A04
On downhill grades, stay alert for large trucks or buses approaching too fast. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0020]
